newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TAIWAN SAYS S.AFRICA SUPPORTS PETROCHEMICAL PLANT.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN SAYS S.AFRICA SUPPORTS PETROCHEMICAL PLANT.

text.p: South Africa had pledged full support for a $3.5 billion joint venture petrochemical plant with Taiwan and was likely to submit its proposal by the end of September, Taiwanese vice-premier Hsu Li-teh said on Tuesday.

Speaking at a luncheon hosted by South Africa's Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo, Hsu said that he was encouraged by the South African government's support for the 50-50 partnership plan, but he added that he was cautious not to pre-empt a deal.

"We feel heartened that the South African government has pledged its full support... Of course the project is so huge and there are so many factors involved, one should not count the eggs before they are hatched," he said.

"A petrochemical complex has been proposed to your government and businessmen. I think the chance is quite promising. I understand they are going to give us a proposal before the end of September," Hsu added.
He said that if the project went ahead Taiwanese experts calculated that a total of 80,000 jobs could be created.

South Africa's Nzo told reporters that the 48 member Taiwanese delegation had also signed an agreement on a social forestry project valued at $5 million and a memorandum of understanding on education for which Taiwan would contribute about 25 million rand.
"The visit has been important from the point of view not only of firming up our relations but also the results of the visit will of course benefit our country," Nzo said.
Hsu said that Taiwan was eager to work within South Africa's economy because of its strategic position.

"South Africa is a rich country. We anticipate you are going to have a vital role to play in the future, especially in the Asian region. You are destined to become the powerhouse, the locomotive, the operation centre of all Africa, and it is our selfish interest to join hands with you and become strategic partners in your development," he said.
